## Search it yourself

`deja` with no arguments opens a terminal search across every agent's history — starting with
the se
ssions behind your uncommitted changes, then recent work in the current project.
- **Navigate:** `↑↓` picks a session, `↵` opens at the match, `/` searches inside a session, `]` `[`

jump between turns, `^s` toggles date/relevance sort (`deja search --sort date`).
- **Filter:** by

agent (`codex:`), time (`today`, `yesterday`, `week`, `month`), or project (`in:<project>`).
- **Res
ume or hand off:** `r` reopens the session in its native agent; `o` continues it in another agent wi

th its goal, decisions and open work.
- **Recover deleted chats:** `tab` switches between this proje
ct, all projects, and **Deleted** (sessions an agent purged that deja still holds); `R` restores one
, `D` deletes (`deja delete <id>`), `?` lists all keys.
Prefer a browser? `deja view` exports the store — sessions, the recall audit trail, and promoted not
es — into one local HTML file (try the live demo). With `DEJA_TUI=0` (or `deja brief`), `deja` print
s a plain-text summary.
## Highlights
- **Starts full on day one.** Months of existing transcripts across all forty-three agents are searc

hable immediately — fix a bug in Codex and Claude Code, Cursor or OpenCode recalls it.
- **Automatic
recall via hooks & MCP.** Surfaces prior sessions at session start, before a file edit or command r

uns, and when a command fails.
- **Survives compaction.** Over 43 measured compactions, summaries ke

pt 77% of decisions and 0.2% of commands; deja hands back the rest (how).
- **Indexes code changes,
not just chat.** Tracks opened files, commands with exit codes, and exact `Edit` spans (`deja blame

<file>:<line>`, `deja restore <path>`).
- **Tracks decision lifecycle & staleness.** `deja promote <
id> --state rejected` marks a reverted approach so later hits warn why it was dropped (`--state acce

pted` takes the mark back), and hits report when files touched by a session have changed since.
- **
Travels with the repository.** `deja repo add` commits the decisions and dead ends you pick into `.d

eja/memory.jsonl`; a teammate's agent recalls them after a clone (repo memory).
- **Local and privat
e by default.** Zero LLM calls, no cloud account, and automatic credential redaction at index time (
ult.** Zero LLM calls, no cloud account, and automatic credential redaction at index time (privacy).
### Your own work, wrapped
`deja stats --card` draws your yearly agent activity in the terminal or writes an SVG for your GitHu
b profile (convert to PNG in browser).
## Install
`install.sh` places the `deja` binary in `~/.local/bin`, and `deja install --auto` wires MCP recall
and hooks into every detected agent and builds the initial index (~10s).
[该节后续省略]
## Privacy

Indexing and search are local. The network is used only by `deja update`, `deja sync ssh`,
the versi

on check in `deja doctor`, `deja embed` against an endpoint you configure (and,
once it has built th

e semantic sidecar, each search, which sends the query to that
endpoint), and a once-a-day look at t

he latest release from an interactive command. That look sends no
session data; `DEJA_OFFLINE=1` tur

ns it off, and so does `DEJA_NO_UPDATE_NOTICE` set to any
value, which also hides the note a new ver
sion prints on its first run.

Credentials are stripped as the index is built: cloud and provider keys, tokens and JWTs,
PEM blocks

, passwords in URLs or stated in prose. Each becomes `[redacted:<kind>]` and the
text around it stay

s searchable. The source transcripts still hold them
(one machine had 84 in 42 sessions):
`deja secr

ets` names those sessions without printing a value, and `deja secrets --scrub`
rewrites the ones it
can, keeping the original beside the file.

`deja forget` drops sessions and keeps them dropped across rebuilds. `~/.config/deja/exclude`
skips

a project per line, or a whole store with `harness:opencode`. The
security model has the data flows
and what redaction cannot catch.
## How it works

Local inverted index in `~/.cache/deja`: parse the JSONL and SQLite stores, redact
credentials, writ

e an append-only `records.bin` plus token buckets, and track per-file state in
`manifest.gob` so rep

eat runs only ingest what changed. The MCP server, stats, share and
sync all read that one index. De
tails in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.
